First, we factor the numerator:

$$
\frac{{cos}^{4}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }=\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }
$$

Next, we use the Pythagorean identity to rewrite the expression in the parentheses, and then we simplify the resulting expression as much as possible:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot 1+{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{2\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{2\cdot \cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }}{\cancel{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{2}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =2\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{cos}^{4}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }=2\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta .
$$
